title: FAA national ground stop: telecommunications / SMART boundary investigation
epistemic_rule: Publicly documented statements and news reports are not live FAA telemetry. No inferred causal edge may be promoted without an attributable independent source and observable evidence.

findings.text: The FAA introduced the AI-supported SMART platform in September 2026; it combines around 200 data streams into an advisory planning system.
On Nov 10 the FAA announced expansion of SMART's use to airspace managed by all 22 centers; the announcement alone does not establish exact deployment times or code changes per center.

The FAA described a centrally based SMART team passing validated planning recommendations through the Air Traffic Control System Command Center for local consideration; this does not establish operation of pilot/controller radio systems.
Nov 13 nationwide ground stop followed communications problems affecting regional ATC systems; investigators had not established the initial fault/cause at the time of this case capture.
Officials said investigators would examine whether SMART's rollout played a role, without establishing any connection.

Microsoft 365 experienced a separate Nov 12 service incident. Status notes describe unresponsive servers, shifted load and network/configuration investigations. Shared infrastructure with FAA is not demonstrated.

public_known_path: FAA SMART specialists in Washington DC
topology.separate_path: Pilot-controller telecommunications (precise topology unpublished in these sources)

competing_hypotheses.label: Independent telecom infrastructure malfunction
competing_hypotheses.test: Obtain FAA incident timeline, network carrier faults and radio gateway logs; verify first failure preceded any SMART dependency.
competing_hypotheses.disproves: Traceable prior SMART-associated change is necessary for the failure

competing_hypotheses.label: Shared support-service/configuration dependency
competing_hypotheses.test: Compare IAM/DNS/network routing/time sync/change control between SMART and voice/backhaul layers; require specific common component and matching fault times.
competing_hypotheses.disproves: Documented isolation and unchanged shared services during onset

competing_hypotheses.label: SMART-associated load or integration interaction
competing_hypotheses.test: Compare authenticated production deployment timing, telemetry and change windows with first communications failures; seek repeatable mechanism.
competing_hypotheses.disproves: System isolation plus independent telecom failure reproduces without SMART

competing_hypotheses.label: External interference or cyberattack
competing_hypotheses.test: Await investigation with signatures, artefacts, forensic network records and attribution; avoid treating absence of early indication as proof of impossibility.

competing_hypotheses.label: Shared Microsoft dependency
competing_hypotheses.test: Identify actual FAA operational reliance on impacted Microsoft services or a common lower-layer network provider, with timestamp correlation and topology.
competing_hypotheses.disproves: Demonstrated separate infrastructure and distinct initiating faults

eightfold: Compress shared scope versus actual components
Integrate distinct Microsoft incident without conflation
Return with append-only revisions and receipts
Transcend via resilience and fail-independent design
withness: Protect people and safety-critical operational decisions; no speculative causal declaration; no automated aircraft control action.
acceptance: Source-backed facts retain exact links, dates and evidence labels.
No source establishes a causal SMART-to-telecom or Microsoft-to-FAA edge.
Public announcement scope is not treated as deployment/runtime proof.
Actual instrument logs are marked unavailable, not fabricated.
No live Wayglass runtime, deployment or independent model voice is claimed.
Later findings append a correction with provenance rather than overwrite this snapshot.
unknowns: Exact onset, failure domain and first failing component
Which centre subsystems/frequencies/pathways failed versus survived
Which shared services, if any, are used between SMART and ATC communications
Precise SMART change/release times and rollback or isolation results
Whether Microsoft and FAA used any common affected operational infrastructure
